evidence: decorative_mascot: Data perches on top of whatever mark is there: the block stack (hook@0.3 to seg0:end), the 48% bar (seg1:end), the 27.3M bar (seg2:end), the NJ bubble (seg3:mid) and the scale pan (seg4). He cheers with his arms up and never does anything that relates to the number.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg3:mid and seg3:end show two circles, New Jersey and the national average. Inside the NJ circle, '68.1%' is dark text on a light-blue fill with a doubled or smeared outline, so it is the least legible text in the video. Data just stands on top of the circle with his arms up.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The label is in INK on a light accent fill and seems to be drawn twice (stroke plus fill offset). The machine is generic: area circles would work for any comparison, and nothing about them is a map or a passport. The mascot is parked on the mark instead of acting.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Make the NJ value text high-contrast and draw it once, with no duplicate stroke. Replace the circles with something made of the subject: a stack of passports, or a row of 100 people where 68 hold passports for NJ and 48 for the US, filling side by side. Give Data a bit, such as handing out passports until NJ hits 68.
